description: A single-panel X-ray diffraction (XRD) figure consisting of four vertically offset (stacked) intensity traces drawn on one common set of axes: x = 2θ/(°) spanning 30 to 100 with major ticks at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 and 5° subdivisions, y = Intensity/a.u. with no numeric scale (arbitrary units). From bottom to top the traces are 3Cr (black), 2Ni (red), 2Ni3Cr (blue) and 2Ni5Cr (green). Five reflections are annotated on the topmost (2Ni5Cr) trace and their positions are shared by all four patterns: γ(111) between the 40° and 50° gridlines, γ(200) close to the 50° gridline, γ(220) between the 70° and 80° gridlines, γ(311) just below the 90° gridline and γ(222) just above 90°. Every trace consists of exactly this same set of five face-centred cubic austenite peaks with no extra reflection: γ(111) is by far the strongest, γ(200) the second strongest, while γ(220), γ(311) and γ(222) are weak. No reflection attributable to a B2/BCC phase is present in any pattern. The figure therefore demonstrates that 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr are all single-phase FCC γ austenite, in agreement with the caption's and citing text's statement that these steels are fully recrystallized, single equiaxed FCC γ with no B2 phase found.

observations.observation: The figure is a stacked (vertically offset) XRD plot of four traces, labelled from bottom to top 3Cr (black), 2Ni (red), 2Ni3Cr (blue) and 2Ni5Cr (green).
The x-axis is labelled 2θ/(°) and runs from 30 to 100 with tick labels at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100; the y-axis is labelled Intensity/a.u. with no numeric scale.

Five reflections are indexed on the patterns as γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311) and γ(222); γ(111) lies between the 40° and 50° gridlines, γ(200) close to the 50° gridline, γ(220) between the 70° and 80° gridlines, γ(311) just below 90° and γ(222) just above 90°.
All four traces contain the same five peaks and no further reflection, and γ(111) is the strongest peak in each, with γ(200) second strongest and γ(220), γ(311), γ(222) weak.
No B2 phase with body-centred cubic structure is identified in any of the four traces.
Peak heights of the four traces are not quantitatively comparable, because the patterns are plotted with a vertical offset for display.
The caption states the figure is an X-ray diffraction analysis of the 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr steel.

The citing text states that both EBSD and XRD analyses reveal the 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr steels are fully recrystallized, composed of a single equiaxed face-centred cubic (FCC) γ phase with a high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries, with no B2 phase of BCC structure found.

The citing text reports average grain sizes (excluding twin boundaries) of 7.63 μm, 8.95 μm, 8.57 μm and 7.60 μm for the 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr steels, and 3.51 μm, 3.73 μm, 3.72 μm and 2.2 μm when twin boundaries are included; these values are not shown in this figure.
